newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul Shinhwa limit-high on sales news.
newsitem.headline: Seoul Shinhwa limit-high on sales news.

text.p: Shares of Shinhwa Co, a small telecommunications equipment producer, went limit-high on Friday after the company announced an ambitious sales plan.
Shinhwa rose 1,400 won to its daily limit of 19,400.
Shinhwa said its sales would reach 180 billion won this year from 35 billion in 1996, helped by the development of a communication and tracking device for vehicles.
"The stock looks quite promising. Its strength is likely to continue for the time being," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.

A Shinhwa official said the company would begin marketing in late March the Tacho Global Positioning System (TGPS), which it had developed over the past three years. The system allows control centres to track and communicate with vehicles.
Shinhwa, also a producer of leather goods, said it had already received 75,000 orders for the system from bus, taxi and shipping companies.
The unit price was set at around two million won.
